newsitem.title: POLAND: Handlowy sees BWR net up 48 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Handlowy sees BWR net up 48 pct in 1996.

text.p: The brokerage unit of Polish Bank Handlowy SA sees Bank Wspolpracy Regionalnej SA's (BWR) net profit rising to 4.9 million zlotys in 1996 and to 5.8 million in 1997, Handlowy said in a report.
BWR recorded a net profit of 3.3 million zlotys in 1995.

Handlowy said the strengthening position of the bank in southern Poland and its high quality credit portfolio would allow it to increase interest income to 22.3 million zlotys in 1996 and to 29.6 million in 1997 from 15.6 million last year.

"In our opinion, the bank's capital commitments in various entities operating on the financial market will undoubtedly contribute to strengthening the position of BWR in one of the most important economic regions of Poland," it said.

The report, dated August 23 when BWR was at 3.9 zlotys per share, was released to the press on Monday, when the stock closed at 3.95 zlotys. Handlowy said BWR's price-earnings ratio would rise to 13.3 at year-end from 10.3 on August 23.
Handlowy did not give Krakow-based BWR a recommendation because it acts as the stock exchange specialist for the bank's shares.
